data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's failure mode becomes a required precondition for the subject's acceptance \u2014 the shown-to-fail-first installation makes the failure part of the subject's identity, so the test cannot describe what the subject would have been without it.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the same mutation loss occurs under a describe-only installation, the shown-to-fail-first precondition is not doing the work.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If ordinarily-guarded modules show the same loss distribution, the installation ritual is not the differentiator.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the confound of one author and one week explains the distribution, the claim is weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 loss is an artefact of the mutation proposal process rather than the installation, the constraint mechanism is misattributed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under shown-to-fail-first, the subject is not accepted until it has failed the test and been repaired. The repair is part of the subject's construction, so the test is a constraint on the repair process. The 3-of-26 result and the 1/9 compile.py loss reflect that only mutations aligned with the planted failure mode were constrained; mutations outside that mode were described but not constrained.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
